rows.text: The bounded lookup produced two writer candidates whose text reproduces the observed file naming, column set and clean_rel exactly. This upgrades the producer status from not-identified to CANDIDATE_FAMILY_ONLY. It is not an execution certificate for the three dated files.

Both candidate bodies also write a P6_factor_reference/adjust_factor copy under a different name pattern. No counterpart of the three P1 names exists there even though the P6 directory exists, so that predicted sibling is not evidence for these three files.

All three P1 mtimes are 2026-10-17, not the 20260831/20260901/20260925 stamps in the names. The stamps come from the writing code; the mtimes reflect a later copy. Neither is treated as a date authority.

The int64 axis has 300 distinct ordinals with 17-18 rows each. The batch=200 request logic in the candidate bodies would produce a different grouping, so the exact mechanism that produced these 300 groups is recorded as unresolved rather than inferred.

The normative domain contract requires factor (not fq) on price_fq_factor and is silent on fq placement, request binding and enforcement. The earlier "no physical fq column" statement is therefore descriptive only; it is not a contract violation and no allowance is invented.

The dtype contract declares date storage as date with YYYY-MM-DD and nullable N. The two RAW files store int64 and the R33 files store timestamp[ns]. Both are recorded as observations; nothing is converted or normalized.
No date was inferred from any filename, no ordinal was interpreted, no alternate date field was substituted, no factor was filled, no fq column was added and no product was admitted.
